d_sv_content.name: Novel Immunotherapy for Cats with Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
d_sv_content.tagline: Help Investigate a novel immunotherapy for cats with oral squamous cell carcinoma
d_sv_content.description: The purpose of this study is to test a new immunotherapy treatment that is injected directly into the tumor. Researchers want to find out how well the treatment works and how safe it is in cats.
d_sv_content.requirements: There will be 4 immunotherapy injections directly into the tumor. These treatments will be given while under anesthesia and will happen once every 3 weeks.CT scans of the head will be done:Before the first treatmentAt the third treatmentThree weeks after the fourth treatment These scans help doctors see how the tumor is responding to the treatment.Small samples of the tumor (biopsies) will be collected:Before treatment beginsAt the third treatmentBlood samples will be collected:At the first treatmentAt the third treatmentThree weeks after the last treatmentA blood gas test (a special blood test that measures oxygen and other values in the blood) will be done:At the second treatmentAt the fourth treatmentParticipation in the study will end at the Day 84 visit, which takes place 3 weeks after the fourth and final treatment.
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Follow the study's schedule and attend all appointments required as part of the studyYou will be responsible for the costs of any tests needed to diagnose squamous cell carcinoma, as well as any other tests that your pet’s cancer doctor (oncologist) recommends
d_sv_content.whoCan: Cats May Be Able to Join This Study If They:Have been diagnosed with oral squamous cell carcinoma in the gums, tongue, lips, or jaw.Have a tumor that can be reached safely for the study injections.Do not have cancer that has spread beyond the nearby lymph nodes.Have healthy liver and kidney function and do not have any serious health problems.Are healthy enough to be put under anesthesia several times during the study.Are not taking medications that suppress the immune system.Can come to Colorado State University (CSU) for all study-related appointments and visits.
d_sv_content.benefits: Possible Benefits:The treatment may help shrink the tumor or make it go away completely.Possible Risks and Side Effects:The injection site may become slightly swollen or red.Some cats may seem tired (lethargic) or have a decreased appetite for about 24 hours or a little longer after treatment.Because the treatments are given under general anesthesia, there is a small risk of changes in kidney function or heart function.To help reduce these risks, cats will receive fluids and will be carefully monitored by experienced veterinary staff during anesthesia.In very rare cases, anesthesia can cause a cat's heart or breathing to stop.
d_sv_content.compensation:
Funding is available to cover the tests needed to find out if your pet qualifies for the study. These tests may include: a complete blood count (CBC), blood chemistry testing, urine testing, lymph node aspirates, chest X-rays

If your pet is accepted into the study, all study-related costs will be covered, including: veterinary exam fees, blood tests, anesthesia, immunotherapy injections, and CT scans, and biopsies. There is also up to $1,000 is available to help pay for the treatment of any side effects that may occur as a result of study procedures.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: There are 5 visits for the trial which occur every 3 weeks. The study is complete after the Day 84 visit.
